title: Annotatio V §.IV close: Oral (if true) lesser testamentary good — not faith-fundamental; Luke 22:29–30 — stop before §.V
pass_a_gloss: (2) Let us posit that discrimination is to be made between Testamentary Goods and the Commodities arising thence — although otherwise Goods and Commodities well conspire with each other, and Goods can also be called by the name of Commodities and conversely Commodities by the name of Goods — yet the Author will have placed this with me beyond doubt: that Testamentary goods, if speech is of them all indiscriminately, are not of the same reason and weight, and that some of them have a necessary, others a less necessary, connection with eternal salvation; and this being placed beyond doubt, I even call the Disputator himself as arbiter: Whether the Oral Eating of Christ’s body, even if it were true, considered by itself alone, is to be numbered among Testamentary goods of the prior, or rather of the posterior, kind? But if Oral Eating, if it be true, pertains to Testamentary Goods of the posterior kind (as from the said hypothesis it becomes clear that it pertains altogether to these, not to the prior — because from the Author’s other hypothesis many eat Christ’s Body Oraliter who yet perish eternally), it certainly stands that the Doctrine of Oral Eating is not fundamental to the Christian faith, and consequently dissent in this Doctrine is not a fundamental dissent of Faith — and so much the less, the more it is agreed among those so dissenting that the Spiritual Eating of Christ’s body, even apart from all Sacramental, suffices to obtaining eternal salvation — nay, while it completes intimate Union and Communion with Christ, it affords the firstfruits of that eternal life bequeathed by testament from Christ to those spiritually eating Christ’s Body: Whither pertains that said by Christ a little after the Institution of the Sacred Supper to His disciples who had used spiritual Eating: And I assign to you by Testament a Kingdom, that you may eat and drink at my table in my Kingdom, Luke 22:29–30.
pass_b_english: §.IV close: even granting a goods/commodities split, and that testamentary goods differ in weight toward eternal salvation — Oral, if true, belongs to the lesser class (many oral eaters still perish).

So Oral doctrine is not faith-fundamental; dissent here is not fundamental dissent — the more so as spiritual eating apart from sacramental suffices for eternal life and already gives its firstfruits (Luke 22:29–30: kingdom by testament to eat and drink at His table). Stop before Annotatio V §.V.
source_text: (2) Ponamus, inter Bona Testamentaria, & Commoda inde oriunda, discriminandum, cùm alias Bona, & Commoda, probe inter se conspirent, Bonaque etiam Commodorum nomine, & vice versâ Commoda nomine Bonorum, appellari queant, tamen istud extra dubium mecum posuerit Autor, Testamentaria bona, si de iis indiscriminatim omnibus sermo sit, non esse ejusdem rationis & ponderis, eorumque alia necessariam, alia minùs necessariam cum salute æterna habere connexionem; hôcque extra dubium positô, vel ipsum arbitrum appello Disputatorem: Num Oralis Manducatio corporis Christi, etiamsi vera foret, per se solam considerata, prioris, an verò posterioris potiùs generis bonis Testamentariis annumeranda veniat? Quodsi a. ad posterioris generis Bona Testamentaria, Oralis Manducatio, si vera sit, pertinet, (quemadmodum ex dictâ hypothesi, ad hæc omnino, non autem priora, pertinere ex eo manifestum evadit, quòd; ex aliâ Autoris hypothesi, multi Oraliter Corpus Christi manducent, qui æternum tamen pereant) utique constat, Doctrinam de Orali Manducatione non esse fidei Christianæ fundamentalem & per consequens, dissensum in hac Doctrina, non esse dissensum Fidei fundamentalem, tantóque minùs; quanto inter ita dissidentes, magis convenit, Spiritualem Manducationem corporis Christi, etiam citra omnem Sacramentalem, ad salutem æternam obtinendam sufficere, quin, dum intimam hæc cum Christo Unionem Communionémque absolvit, vitæ eam æternæ, Spiritualiter Corpus Christi manducantibus testamento à Christo legatæ, primitias præbere: Quorsum pertinet istud, paulò post Institutionem S. Cœnæ, discipulis suis, spirituali Manducatione usis, à Christo dictum: Kagō diatithemai hymin basileian &c. Et ego vobis Testamento addico Regnum, ut edatis & bibatis ad mensam meam in Regno meo, Luc. 22, 29. & 30.
